# Lark of Training (`lark-of-training`)

Checks required compliance training per role and work state (HIPAA, fraud waste and abuse, Texas HB 300 and others you list): new hires past their deadline, courses never completed, refreshers overdue and courses coming due, with totals by course and department. Staff names are masked before results reach the model.

**Lark never assigns courses or changes the learning system. Lark never emails staff or managers.**

Kestrel ver 1 · Compliance pack · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`kestrel-core`](../kestrel-core)

```bash
npx -y lark-of-training demo
npx -y lark-of-training mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: Bluewater Family Medicine (a made-up practice) and made-up staff. Any likeness to real people is chance.

- [`roster.csv`](fixtures/roster.csv): active staff in Texas and Oklahoma; the terminated front-desk worker is skipped.
- [`lms-completions.csv`](fixtures/lms-completions.csv): Planted: an HB 300 refresher due within 30 days (T101), a new hire with fraud-and-abuse and HB 300 not due until late November (T102), an Oklahoma worker whose HIPAA refresher is overdue and who needs no HB 300 (T103), a physician with every course current, the course name written differently (T104), and a new hire with nothing done 45 days after hire, so HIPAA is late (T105).
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): HIPAA yearly (30 days for new hires), fraud waste and abuse yearly (90 days), HB 300 every two years for Texas staff (90 days). These are examples; your policy sets the real numbers. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `lark_check` | List staff with required compliance courses overdue, never done or due soon. | runs |
| `lark_write_report` | Write lark-training.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and lark-training.html into out_dir (default kestrel-out/lark). | runs |
| `lark_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `lark_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `lark_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `lark_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `lms_assign` | Lark never assigns courses or changes the learning system. | refused |
| `manager_email_send` | Lark never emails staff or managers. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `lark_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `completions` (required) | Training completions export (LMS) under --root: person, course and completion date |
| `roster` (required) | Active staff roster: person, role, department, hire date and work state |
| `settings` (required) | Settings JSON: courses (name, roles, states, refresher and new-hire days) and warn_days |
| `as_of` | Date to measure deadlines and ages from (YYYY-MM-DD); default today |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx lark-of-training inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Training completions (`completions`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `person_id` (required) | text (masked) | Employee ID, Employee #, Emp ID, Staff ID, Worker ID, Caregiver ID, Badge, Person ID |
| `name` | text (masked) | Employee, Employee Name, Staff, Staff Name, Name, Full Name, Worker, Caregiver |
| `course` (required) | text | Course, Course Name, Training, Module, Title, Assignment |
| `completed` | date | Completed, Completion Date, Date Completed, Completed On, Finished |

### Staff roster (`roster`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `person_id` (required) | text (masked) | Employee ID, Employee #, Emp ID, Staff ID, Worker ID, Caregiver ID, Badge, Person ID |
| `name` | text (masked) | Employee, Employee Name, Staff, Staff Name, Name, Full Name, Worker, Caregiver |
| `role` | text | Role, Job Title, Title, Position, Job, Discipline, Job Code |
| `department` | text | Department, Dept, Unit, Location, Site, Cost Center, Clinic |
| `hire_date` | date | Hire Date, Start Date, Date Hired, Hired, Original Hire Date |
| `work_state` | text | Work State, State, Location State |
| `status` | text | Status, Employment Status, State, Current Status |

## Settings file (`lark_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `courses` (required) | Required courses |
| `warn_days` | Days ahead to remind; default 30 |

## Memory

`lark_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `lark_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `kestrel-core` and `remedy-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "lark-of-training": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "lark-of-training",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add lark-of-training -- npx -y lark-of-training mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
lark-of-training tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
lark-of-training sources               # the columns each input is read from
lark-of-training inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
lark-of-training call lark_check '{"completions":"<completions>","roster":"<roster>","settings":"<settings>"}'
lark-of-training eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
lark-of-training demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
